title: The section algebra of a line module on a space restricts correctly to etale bases
statement: Let $S,T$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space], let $f:X\to T$ be a quasi-compact separated morphism over $S$ in the terminology of [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local], and let $L$ be a line module on $X$. On small etale sites, write $L^{\otimes d}$ for the tensor powers ($L^{\otimes0}=\mathcal O_X$), write $f_*$ for direct image, and write $f^*$ for its left adjoint on modules, the tensor pullback along the morphism of ringed etale topoi. There is a quasi-coherent graded Zariski $\mathcal O_T$-algebra $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}f_*L^{\otimes d}$ [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra] [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]: this equality is interpreted through the equivalence between quasi-coherent Zariski and small etale modules on $T$. For every etale scheme map $g:T'\to T$, put $X'=X\times_TT'$, let $f':X'\to T'$ be projection, and let $L'$ be the restriction of $L$ to $X'$. There is a canonical graded isomorphism $g^*\mathcal A\simeq\bigoplus_{d\geq0}f'_* (L')^{\otimes d}$, where on the left $g^*$ is scheme module pullback [def-pc-module-pullback]. Under this isomorphism, the pullback to $X'$ of the evaluation map $f^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_{d\geq0}L^{\otimes d}$ is the evaluation map for $(f',L')$. If $X'$ is a scheme, these direct images and evaluation maps agree with the ordinary Zariski ones for its invertible module [def-sc-invertible-module].

source.place: Tag 03M9 (lemma-pushforward) and the preceding discussion of representable pushforward; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03LX (lemma-pushforward-etale-base-change-modules). Apply degreewise; multiplication and evaluation use the canonical restriction comparisons.

proof.text: Put $F_d=L^{\otimes d}$, with $F_0=\mathcal O_X$. On an etale cover trivializing $L$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space], every $F_d$ is identified with $\mathcal O$ by multiplying the tensor factors [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. On that cover it therefore has the local presentation $0\to0\to\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\sim}F_d\to0$, where the displayed isomorphism is the chosen trivialization (and for $d=0$ the canonical one). This is a local free presentation, so each $F_d$ is quasi-coherent by [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module].

Apply [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-quasi-coherent-pushforward] to $f$ and each $F_d$. The hypotheses are exactly the assumed quasi-compactness and separation of $f$; no representability of $X$ is used. It gives a quasi-coherent etale module $f_*F_d$. Apply the inverse equivalence in [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] on the scheme $T$, obtaining a quasi-coherent Zariski module $A_d$ whose associated etale module is canonically $f_*F_d$. Its sections on a Zariski open $V$ are the compatible sections of $F_d$ on $X\times_TV$.

source.place: Tag 03M9 (lemma-pushforward), and preceding scheme comparison through descent.tex Tags 03DX,03LC; section interpretation as in Tag 03M8 (lemma-compute-pushforward), proof.

proof.text: For each open $V\subseteq T$ and $s\in A_m(V)$, $t\in A_d(V)$, multiply their compatible local sections using $L^{\otimes m}\otimes L^{\otimes d}\to L^{\otimes(m+d)}$. This produces a section $st\in A_{m+d}(V)$ and commutes with restrictions, since tensor multiplication does so on every etale chart. Associativity, commutativity, bilinearity and the unit $\mathcal O_T\to A_0$ follow by multiplying local coefficients in a trivialization of $L$; the unit is pullback of functions. Hence these operations give the graded algebra of [def-weil-pbc-graded-sheaf-structures]. Let $\mathcal A=\bigoplus_{d\geq0}A_d$ in Zariski module sheaves. It is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-coproduct-closure], so is a quasi-coherent algebra by [def-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-algebra]. The equivalence of [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence] identifies this sum with $\bigoplus_d f_*F_d$: restriction to the Zariski opens of that etale coproduct is the indicated sum, because sheaf tensor pullback defining the forward comparison preserves coproducts by its left-adjoint property [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction].

source.place: Tag 0D3C (lemma-descending-property-ample), section-algebra paragraph; schemes.tex Tag 01ID for coproduct closure; sites-modules.tex Tag 03D7 for the pullback adjunction.

proof.text: For each degree, the adjunction [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction] gives the counit $\epsilon_d:f^*f_*F_d\to F_d$, corresponding to the identity of $f_*F_d$. In the tensor description it sends a local generator $a\otimes s$ to $a\,s|_W$ on a chart $W\to X$ lying over the domain of $s$. This formula follows by taking the identity map through the inverse-image and extension-of-scalars Hom bijections: the latter sends a map $v$ to $a\otimes s\mapsto a\,v(s)$. Form the direct sum of these counits. Pullback preserves coproducts: for every module $H$, the adjunction identifies maps out of $f^*(\bigoplus_d A_d)$ with $\prod_d\operatorname{Hom}(f^*A_d,H)$. This gives the displayed evaluation $\psi:f^*\mathcal A\to\bigoplus_dF_d$. On local tensors $\psi((a\otimes s)(b\otimes t))=ab\,(st)|_W=(a\,s|_W)(b\,t|_W)$, and the unit goes to the unit, so it is a homomorphism of graded algebras.

source.place: Tag 0D3C, natural maps psi_d and the graded adjunction map; sites-modules.tex Tag 03D7 (lemma-adjoint-pullback-pushforward-modules), explicit Hom bijections.

proof.text: Write $h:X\prime\to X$ for the other projection. Since $g$ is etale, [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction] identifies etale tensor pullback by $g$ and $h$ with restriction and gives $g^*(f_*F_d)\simeq f\prime_*(h^*F_d)$ canonically. The tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor], iterated starting from $h^*\mathcal O_X=\mathcal O_{X\prime}$, identifies $h^*F_d$ with $(L\prime)^{\otimes d}$ for every $d$. By the pullback comparison in [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], the left side corresponds to ordinary scheme pullback $g^*A_d$. Thus the degreewise comparisons are isomorphisms $g^*A_d\simeq f\prime_* (L\prime)^{\otimes d}$, with the right side interpreted in the same Zariski equivalence. Pullback preserves the sum by the Hom argument of Step 4, so their sum is the required isomorphism of graded modules.

Check the operations under this isomorphism. For an etale scheme $V\to T\prime$, the comparison of [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction] sends a section represented on $X\times_TV$ to that same section on $X\prime\times_{T\prime}V$, the identical space. Consequently it sends $st$ to $s|\,t|$, and sends the pulled-back function defining the unit to the same function. It is therefore an isomorphism of graded algebras, not just modules. On a chart $W\to X\prime$, the restriction of the degree-$d$ evaluation of Step 4 and the evaluation formed for $f\prime$ both send $a\otimes s$ to $a\,s|_W$. The pullback comparison in [lem-trf-space-etale-module-pushforward-restriction] identifies tensor pullbacks along the two paths by keeping that section and multiplying coefficients. Equality on these local generators gives equality of the sheaf maps in every degree, hence equality on the coproduct. This proves the asserted evaluation compatibility.

source.place: Tag 0D3C, sentence asserting pullback compatibility of psi_d; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03LX and its pullback footnote. The local tensor computation is written out.

proof.text: Finally suppose that $X\prime$ is a scheme. Apply [lem-trf-space-qc-separated-etale-local] to the jointly surjective etale family $\{\mathrm{id}_T:T\to T,\ g:T\prime\to T\}$: its forward implication shows that $f\prime$ is quasi-compact and separated. By [lem-trf-scheme-zariski-etale-quasi-coherent-equivalence], the line module $L\prime$ corresponds to an ordinary invertible module, tensor pullback agrees with ordinary scheme tensor pullback, and the direct images of its tensor powers agree with Zariski direct images. The tensor powers themselves correspond: on an open trivializing the invertible module both versions are $\mathcal O$, and their transition maps are the $d$-th powers of the same units. On every open of $T\prime$, the comparison of direct images is the identity on sections; consequently their multiplication is the same product of sections. The ordinary counit and the etale counit both send $a\otimes s$ to $a\,s|_W$ on local tensors over open subschemes of $X\prime$. Thus their evaluation maps agree, as do their sums. This also covers $X\prime=X$ when $X$ was a scheme to begin with.

source.place: Discussion preceding Tag 03M9; descent.tex Tags 03DX,03LC(1),(3),05VG. Separation and quasi-compactness after etale base change: spaces-morphisms.tex Tags 03KG,03KM.

lean.statement: theorem space_section_algebra_etale_base_change (S : Scheme.{u}) (T : Over S) (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : X.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj T) (hqc : IsQuasiCompactPresheafMap f) (hsep : IsSeparatedPresheafMap f) (L : X.Modules) (hL : X.IsLineModule L) : ∃ A : SpaceSectionAlgebra f (lineTestFamily X L hL), A.AgreesWithSchemes ∧ ∀ (T' : Over S) (g : T' ⟶ T) (_ : Etale g.left) (F' : (Over S)ᵒᵖ ⥤ Type u) (h : F' ⟶ X.obj.obj) (f' : F' ⟶ yoneda.obj T') (_ : IsPullback h f' f (yoneda.map g)), ∃ A' : SpaceSectionAlgebra f' ((lineTestFamily X L hL).pullback h), Nonempty (SpaceSectionAlgebraBaseChange h g A A') ∧ A'.AgreesWithSchemes
lean.note: The actual cartesian scheme-test realization of the given small-etale line module is reused. SpaceSectionAlgebra bundles the compatible-section limit universal property, homogeneous products, sheaf coproduct, and tensor-adjunction evaluation. Base change is fixed on every local tensor generator, with explicit graded multiplication/unit and total-sum comparison. The final predicate identifies ordinary Zariski direct image by the section-normalized counit. These are helpers of this same section-algebra statement, not freely chosen maps or a substitute line module.
